arm_descriptions.description: the settings every committed ALFWorld number was measured under: a choice between two places the robot rates exactly the same is settled by their names, largest last
that choice is settled instead by a key derived from the hunt's own identity, so it carries no information and two runs of one game agree
that choice takes the head of the planner's own list, i.e. the smallest name. An upper bound on what a lucky name order is worth on this benchmark, reported as that and not as a candidate default
the seeded choice, and a blind hunt that starts from the robot's own record of where things of the target's kind have turned up, learned on the training split only

grading: the game judges its own success; a cell's number is the games it won of the games it played
training: the record of where kinds of things turn up was learned on valid_train only, in one pass, from finds the robot made and the game confirmed; every evaluation run loads it read only
